notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase for the data-handling and disclosure Considerations of Policy 1.20 (coder A general, coder B during-work), resolved as during-work because they are action directives, while Context sentences and definitions stay general; (2) actor for template and policy-scope sentences (instructor vs admin vs all), resolved by who the sentence addresses; (3) type choices where a sentence mixes two ideas (P31 vs P52 for output evaluation, P35 vs P63 for testing assignments in AI, P06 vs P01 for the Conditional template's ban on other coursework, P47 vs P48 for the working group's own AI-use note), resolved by re-reading the passage and the type definitions; (4) modality for descriptive sentences (may vs informs). Unit-count differences: coder A coded each of three syllabus templates' repeated sentences separately (10 exact repeats, dropped); coder B split some sentences into pieces (integrity page 3 pieces of one sentence, the 25% threshold) which were folded back; three B-only items judged not to be a separate policy were dropped (a resource-availability line, a revision-history note, an in-sentence tool-name list). Real one-coder finds were kept (A: 2, the rationale clause and the legal-understanding duty; B: several split-out rules such as opt-out and 'use is permitted'). The reconciler added one unit neither coder found. Unit stance was set by one rule across all units and not compared between coders.
